title: Best Video Editors (2026): How to Hire One for YouTube, Reels and Ads
description: How to hire a video editor: what to send, what a package should include, music licensing, and the red flags to check before ordering.
intro: A good editor turns raw footage into something people watch to the end. A poor match costs you days of back-and-forth. Most problems come from unclear expectations about length, style and music, so this guide focuses on settling those before you order.

faq.q: How do I send large video files?
faq.a: Upload your footage to a cloud drive such as Google Drive or Dropbox and share a link with view or download access. Name the clips clearly and include a short note on the order they belong in.

faq.q: Who is responsible for the music?
faq.a: Agree on this before ordering. Either you supply licensed tracks, or the editor uses music from a library they are licensed to use for your purpose. Unlicensed music can get a video muted, blocked or demonetized.

faq.q: Should I hire one editor for long videos and Shorts?
faq.a: Many editors do both, but the skills differ. Long-form editing is about pacing and story; short-form is about the first two seconds, captions and fast cuts. Check the portfolio for the format you need.
Usually a round of notes on the same cut, such as trimming a section or changing a caption. Asking for a completely different style or adding new footage is typically treated as new work.

faq.q: Can I keep working with the same editor?
faq.a: Yes. Once an editor knows your style, later videos are faster and more consistent. Many sellers offer packages for multiple videos per month.
